newsitem.title: USA: American Home to buy Solvay's animal health unit.
newsitem.headline: American Home to buy Solvay's animal health unit.

text.p: American Home Products Corp. said Friday it plans to buy Belgian chemicals group Solvay S.A.'s worldwide animal health business for about $450 million.

The Madison, N.J.-based drug and health care products company said Solvay's animal health business would be combined with American Home's veterinary division, Fort Dodge Animal Health, which is headquartered in Overland Park, Kan.
The company said the acquisition, which it expects to be effective by year end, would raise the worldwide sales of Fort Dodge to about $800 million.
A company spokesman said sales for Fort Dodge were projected to be $470 million in 1996 without the acquisition.
Solvay's product lines will give Fort Dodge a greater market presence in Europe and the Far East, as well as strong entry into the global swine and poultry biological markets, American Home said.
Separately, Solvay said it would spend the proceeds of the sale on acquiring human pharmaceutical product lines or companies in the United States.

Solvay, which will net a a pre-tax capital gain of around $192 million from the sale, also renewed a large credit line with a number of European banks last month, giving it reserves of around $1 billion at its disposal.
"We are not looking, except if an extraordinary opportunity arises, for one mega-acquisition," said Daniel Janssen, Solvay's chief executive officer, at a news conference.
"For the moment we are working on selective acquisitions ... in therapeutic areas where we are strong," he said.
Janssen noted Solvay's share of the pharmaceuticals market in Europe was more than 1 percent in 1995 but only 0.3 percent in the United States. "We want to grow much faster in the U.S," he said.
American Home's stocks was 37.5 cents higher at $63.125 on the New York Stock Exchange in early afternoon trading.
